scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original A1 pilot bank for I Can Try Again; independent questions on the original passage; not pedagogically approved.

tabs.title: Understanding the story
tabs.description: Choose what the story tells us.

questions.q: Why does Mia feel worried on Monday?
choices: She has no English book.
She finds words she does not know.
Her friend is not at school.
She cannot find her notebook.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says that some words in the story are new to Mia, and she feels worried.

questions.q: What does Mia do when she stops reading?
choices: She goes home.
She asks to read another book.
She closes her book for the day.
She puts a question mark by the sentence.
questions.explanation: Mia makes a small question mark next to the sentence about a train.

questions.q: Who helps Mia understand a word with a picture?
choices: Her younger brother.
Her English teacher.
Her friend Leo.
A student from another class.
questions.explanation: Leo shows Mia the picture beside the story, and she understands one word.

questions.q: How does Mia feel when she reads on Friday?
choices: Happy because she understands more.
Angry because she has a new story.
Worried because Leo is not there.
Sad because the book is too long.
questions.explanation: In paragraph three, Mia understands more of the new story and smiles.

questions.q: Why does Mia look in her notebook?
choices: To draw a picture of a train.
To keep the new words for later.
To write the whole story again.
To give the notebook to Leo.
questions.explanation: Mia writes two new words in her notebook after asking about them.

questions.q: What does Leo do instead of telling Mia every answer?
choices: He reads the story for her.
He asks her to stop reading.
He shows her something that may help.
He gives the story to another student.
questions.explanation: Leo helps Mia work out a word from a picture instead of giving every answer.

questions.q: Why can Mia read lines to her brother now?
choices: She has a different teacher.
She knows every word in English.
The teacher gives her a shorter book.
She has practised and understands more.
questions.explanation: Mia practises reading during the week and can read five lines at home.

questions.q: You do not understand one word in a story. What can you do?
choices: Stop reading all English books.
Look at the picture and ask a question.
Copy every word from the book.
Read only the last page.
questions.explanation: Mia learns by looking at a picture and asking for help with a new word.

questions.q: Your first reading is difficult. What is a good next step?
choices: Try reading again slowly.
Say you are bad at English.
Never read that story again.
Wait until you know every English word.
questions.explanation: The story shows that trying again and practising can make reading easier.

questions.q: What does the end of Mia's story show?
choices: She needs Leo to read at home.
She is now the best reader in class.
The first story was very easy.
Small steps can help her read better.
questions.explanation: Mia continues practising and understands more, although the new story is still not easy.
